restatement: Add prompt-shaped markdown tools to the headless template core: a FENCE...END_FENCE block and a fence filter that wrap content in a backtick code fence always longer than any backtick run inside it (with an optional lang from a quoted string or variable path, one leading and one trailing line break trimmed, closing fence plus line break), a heading_offset=N filter that shifts ATX headings outside fenced code with clamping to 1-6, and escape_md inline/block modes where block also neutralises line-start structure. FENCE must behave like any block (unclosed is a located syntax-error, counts toward maxDepth, standalone-line rule), spec and analyze must know the new block and filters, and none of this may change existing test expectations, plain escape_md output, or add runtime dependencies.
verification_plan: Run the gate (fence, heading-offset, escape-modes tests) and the full jest suite plus tsc --noEmit; all must pass
c1: confirm fence length = max(3, longest backtick run + 1), computed without stack-limited spreading, on the rendered body; check one leading/trailing LF (and CRLF) trimmed, empty body, nesting
c2: quoted, path, empty, missing and missing-variable lang; fence filter with and without lang; lang that holds a line break or backtick must not break the opening line
c3: unclosed FENCE located at its tag (incl. nested/later ones), stray END_FENCE, FENCE counted in maxDepth by the parser, FENCE/END_FENCE in the standalone tag set

c4: offsets positive/negative/clamped, non-integer and missing params are type-errors at the variable, fenced code (backtick/tilde, longer fences, unclosed) spared, inline code-span lines not taken as fences, CommonMark ATX forms (indent 0-3, tab) handled
c5 and m2: plain escape_md body is byte-identical to the old function; block adds exactly the listed line-start escapes and no double backslash; invalid/empty/wrong-case modes are type-errors
c6: spec blocks list FENCE/END_FENCE, filters list fence/heading_offset/escape_md modes; analyze counts FENCE and knows the filters via the shared FILTERS list
m1: no pre-existing test file changed; any edit to a frozen test is reported

Goal-critical: try adversarial bodies and langs (backtick runs, CR-only breaks, huge values, injected lang) to see if a fence can close early; check existing templates (no FENCE, plain escape_md) render the same

findings.title: heading_offset skips ATX headings indented by one to three spaces, though its own fence detection honours that indent

serves.scenario: c4 says heading_offset shifts every ATX heading line. In CommonMark an ATX heading may be indented by up to three spaces, and the filter's own fence detection accepts that indent (/^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})/). The heading rewrite only matches /^(#{1,6}) /, so a drafted value with ' # Notes' or '   ## Detail' keeps its level while the headings around it shift. The resulting document hierarchy is wrong (a sub-heading can end up above its parent). A tab after the hashes ('#	Title') is skipped the same way.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test (c4: shifts every ATX heading line)
findings.reproduction:
render('${{ v | heading_offset=1 }}', { v: ' # indented
   ## three
# top' }, { standaloneLines: false }).output is ' # indented
   ## three
## top'. The expected output is ' ## indented
   ### three
## top'. Smallest fix: match /^( {0,3})(#{1,6})(?=[ 	])/ in the rewrite and keep the captured indent.

findings.title: A fence filter lang that contains '=' or ':' is truncated or misparsed by the existing parseFilter

serves.scenario: parseFilter splits the shorthand on every '=', so '${{ v | fence="a=b" }}' silently writes a fence with lang 'a'. A lang that contains ':' switches to named-params parsing. This comes from the pre-existing filter parser, not from the new code, and realistic language tags such as c++ and 'my lang' work. Noted for the lead only.
